A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GROTO study and contain readable main text, equations, Figures 1–9, Tables 1–16, and supplementary Sections 6–15. The additional v4 page reflects pagination changes, not missing research material.

before.justification: v2 reports original GROTO classification experiments, ablations, class-mining and forgetting analyses, and training-cost measurements in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark evaluations and the supplementary DomainNet-126-CI experiment in Section 8 and Table 6.

M1.justification: Section 3 and supplementary Algorithms 1–5 retain identical positive-class mining, prototype selection, feature self-organization, topology distillation, and exemplar replay procedures and losses.

E1.justification: Both evaluate class-incremental adaptation on Office-31-CI, Office-Home-CI, ImageNet-Caltech-CI, and supplementary DomainNet-126-CI. No datasets, domains, tasks, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain ViT-B, CIDA, ProCA-B, PLUE, TPDS, DIFO, LEAD-B, and LCFD. Table 6 retains DIFO and LCFD, and comparator membership in the session, class-mining, visualization, and training-cost comparisons also matches.

E3.justification: The class/session partitions, accuracy metrics, model configurations, optimization settings, and augmentation procedures are unchanged. This includes the supplementary DomainNet protocol and the dataset constructions in Tables 13–14.

E4.justification: Both retain the same loss/component ablations and hyperparameter analyses in Tables 4–5, class-mining analyses in Tables 7–9, forgetting analyses in Tables 10–11, and feature and decision-boundary visualizations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The unchanged standard deviation calculation in Equation 5 concerns prototype selection, not uncertainty in experimental results.

E6.justification: Matched tables, figures, and result passages retain identical numerical values and findings. For example, GROTO's Office-31-CI average remains 93.0% in Table 1, and its DomainNet-126-CI average remains 65.7% in Table 6.

T1.justification: The problem assumptions and definitions, Equations 1–16, and the computational-complexity derivation in supplementary Section 15 are unchanged. No mathematical argument or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same CI-SFUDA problem, two-module GROTO contribution, and state-of-the-art performance claim. The added code-availability sentence does not alter these scientific claims.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and interpretations are unchanged, including Section 10's tradeoff between compatibility with source classifier weights and optimal target-domain discrimination. No new limitation or applicability boundary is introduced.

D1.justification: v4 adds a GROTO code-repository link to the abstract; v2 provides no code-access pointer. Existing pseudocode, hyperparameters, hardware details, dataset-construction information, and training-cost disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: Both retain the same 51 references and research positioning. Changed bibliography back-reference page numbers reflect pagination only.

P1.justification: The abstract gains a brief code-availability sentence, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The remaining wording, terminology, and logical section sequence match after accounting for relocated displays and page breaks.

P2.justification: Figure 2 moves from PDF page 3 to 4, Figure 3 from 7 to 6, and Tables 1–2 from 6 to 7. Graphics, captions, and table structures remain unchanged. Reflow also isolates the acknowledgment continuation on a mostly empty v4 page 9.

improvement.justification: v4's added repository pointer modestly improves implementation discoverability while retaining the scientific content and evidence. Pagination becomes less tidy, particularly the mostly empty acknowledgment-continuation page, but this small presentation drawback does not outweigh the added code-access information.
